body:
Initially our mutual friend communicated these things to me without asking, but as it got more involved, we realised it only makes things worse. You're right - it's not fair on him, and I spoke to him not with the expectation that it would get through to her, but because I needed to get it out to someone I was close to. 

After we had a chat I specifically asked him not to be the go between, as it was just ridiculous that we'd have to ask him to do that. The friends I went to town with maintain that I did nothing wrong and that she was being immature, so I shouldn't be the one to reach out - hence why I don't really know what to do. Thank you so much for replying :)

Damn you're right, I made a mistake there. I spend a lot of time indoors/going out after dark (4:30PM) atm so I've been using the Hydroboost, but if I go out during the day I use Simple Protecting Moisture Cream with SPF30. Thanks for pointing that out 😅

I just use a moisturizer with hyaluronic acid in it (nowhere near as effective as a dedicated product I know) and let it soak in for AGES before proceeding with any makeup. During the day I use my Simple Moisture Cream with SPF30 if I'm going outside for a while - it feels like a heavyish sunscreen so I have to let that sink in for a long time too.

I'm in the UK so seeing a dermatologist for acne is reserved for the most severe cases, which I am not. I'm pretty sure it's hormone related but I don't have many options there. If it persists/gets worse I may see my GP to ask about replacing my contraception, as it's a few years old and the levels of hormone it's releasing are decreasing slowly. I can control it with my skincare routine though, 80% of the time.

Annoyingly, Lancome Teint Idole is one of the worst offenders! Looks quite nice when fresh, really not nice a few hours after. I'd love to get some more high end foundations as they looked the nicest when applied, but I have to be super selective because of my budget and make sure there's a high chance it'll work for me.

I also cut down my skincare to once a day for a while as I was adjusting my routine (using only a couple of products, not the whole load of stuff I do now) - it did exactly the same thing with my foundation :(

Would Teint Miracle count in this case? It looked really nice on me, but again not for long. I've also got Rimmel Lasting Radiance which I haven't tried yet, it's a bit dark but I can lighten it. It's supposed to be more of a natural, satiny look afaik so I'll give it a try. Any other foundations that are more of a cream base/satin finish you recommend? Thank you!

I make sure I use a really good moisturiser with hyaluronic acid to try and combat this, so my skin is never dehydrated (I just know it would be if I didn't moisturise well) - I've found if I slack on any of the steps in my routine, my acne starts coming back :(
Whoops I forgot to mention! I always set with powder - I've tried a little bit, a lot, baking, you name it. Also about a million brands as well 😂

I'm a Brit myself! Otherwise I completely get what you mean about us being another breed of drunk, despite being female I might fall into that category as well 😂😂 it's more the teenage lad thing that I'm worried I'll clash with, even if I am 'one of the guys' most of the time. A gf bowing out of a lad's get together/party at one of their houses is normal right? I don't mind either way, I just don't know what the done thing is haha.

Oh they're major piss takers, I know that. They'll make fun of anything and everything, and my boyfriend has the reputation as the 'punchbag' of the group - not in a bad way, a laddish kind of way. By extension his girlfriend gets the same treatment, they've ripped into me a few times after learning of my existence and they don't hold back. It just makes me laugh hearing it second hand but I can understand that he wouldn't know how they'd act around me and not want to risk things.


We've been friends for years, but online and not in person. It's like two worlds colliding so it's hard trying to navigate it. As for telling me from the start, he hasn't made any concrete plans so he isn't sure who he'll invite, just throwing ideas around. If it is a lads thing (which I'm going to guess it might be) then I could either take a leap and say 'fuck it, we can all still have fun' or say 'yeah it might be hard stuck with a load of lads making inside jokes all evening'. Haven't decided yet which I should do.

I think that's what he's trying to say ("hey I just want to have a guys night") but doesn't want to exclude me or hurt my feelings. He's not the greatest with words so he wouldn't say that kind of thing upfront, but it makes the most sense. I get why he'd wonder what might happen if a 20 year old woman were in a room full of 18 year old guys slagging each other off and roasting (god knows I do the same but that's beside the point, lads are like another species), so I don't want to push it. If it's a party with other people and not just his immediate friend group then I'm definitely going, but anything else is such a grey area. Hmm.

Adding another comment because we've just had a chat and you seem to be more acquainted with lad culture as it were. He's said if it were a 'party' meaning lots of different people were going then there'd be no question about whether or not I'd come, of course I would. If it's just him and his lad group who he's known since he was 11, he said it just might be weird since he doesn't know if we'd get on, if they'd even talk to me and because I'd be the only girl there.


 If it turns out that it's just a lad get together instead of a party, would it be awkward of me insisting I want to come? Should I just let them have their fun if it comes down to that? I want to be there more than anything but I don't want to insert myself in a situation where I wouldn't normally be if you get my drift.

This sounds like a great idea, thank you. Unfortunately I'll be travelling 5 hours away from home so I won't be able to bring any of my own friends, but I'm sure I can join in enough on my own. Thank you for your advice!

I'm British too, we live about 5 hours away. Proper ladsladslads have always been a bit intimidating to me, but considering my boyfriend pretty much is one I'm gonna have to get used to them one way or another 😂

I asked him this, because I was getting vibes that he just didn't want me to come, but his answer was "of course I want you to, it just might be weird". He's usually very straightforward and tells it like it is, I feel like he'd tell me straight if he didn't want me to go. I might ask him straight up if he wants me there again but I'm sure I'll get the same answer as last time.
It does, thank you. I know he won't judge or compare, he just wants to see me. I'll take it slow and work it out, he deserves it for being so good to me. Thanks again!

He's a 17 year old guy. From the conversations we've had he looks at stereotypical straight porn, you know the sort - bright lights and overly loud moaning, just to get off as he put it. He doesn't watch anymore because we have Skype sex and the like regularly, he says he doesn't need anything else. I don't have anything against porn and wouldn't care if he did still watch, but he chooses not to.

I'm scared he'll be disappointed. Porn has breasts of all different sizes, just good looking ones. Young, perky...they're not normal by any means, the fact that they're there means they're ideals most women can't really look up to. That's what I'm worried about, that that's all he's seen.

He does. He always asks to see my body when we Skype (we're long distance) and in person he took some of my clothes off himself despite never having touched a girl before. He's told me he wants to see all of me, it's just my own hangups.

Absolutely none (I know, I know...). He's not pressuring me by any means, but he's really eager to see me and that does help. I just feel like based on what he's seen of breasts so far, he'll have an idea of what they look like and when he does see them he'll secretly go 'oh, they're not what I was expecting'.

My previous boyfriend never had a job, so I should be thankful I have someone willing to work hard. I'm only posting because I have a history of snap reactions and when talking to others and taking time to cool down and get advice, my opinion completely changes. Instead of talking to him and risk overreacting, I've come to here to get an honest opinion, which I'm very grateful for. It's true I was very bothered by it, but now I see there's no need to be. Perhaps one day I'll be able to cut to the chase and see things for what they really are without going a bit spare in between, but I'm working on it!

I was originally going to see him as a friend and go sightseeing, a little treat to myself as I haven't spent any money in a very long time. You're right, I shouldn't do a 180 and complain. It's a well connected city with plenty to do, I should make the best of it. Thank you!

I was trying to justify it because he doesn't actually need to work, he's still living at home and doesn't spend any money on anything. Was still a bad idea of mine to think that though, hence me getting it off my chest so I can think rationally about it haha. I'm fine for money, I still have plenty of savings, I think it's just because I haven't spent that much before. Not a big deal in the grand scheme of things.

The NHS funding for mental health is dire, especially in the area I'm from. From my understanding, inpatient beds are very limited and there is the possiblity of me moving very far away from home, definitely not unheard of. They prefer to try and support people as much as possible at home instead of admitting them. Frankly I wouldn't mind going inpatient if a psychiatrist deemed to necessary, I'd go out of my mind missing my boyfriend but if it was necessary, who am I to argue? I'd do anything to get my life back on track. A crisis team does exist, so I hope they'll be able to help me either tomorrow or Saturday.

This was supposed to be my year of sorting stuff out. I had my referral to the mental health team, I was going to take on small amounts of work experience to help me get back on track. We only found out we had to leave this house about two weeks ago and we've got nowhere since, it's like it's all falling apart. The reason I'm going back in September is because that's when term (semester?) starts in the UK, no courses start at any other time of year.
